newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's Mbeki seeks faster economic reform.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's Mbeki seeks faster economic reform.

text.p: South Africa must accelerate the implementation of the macroeconomic framework for growth, employment and redistribution (GEAR), Deputy President Thabo Mbeki said on Monday.

Mbeki, who is almost certain to succeed President Nelson Mandela in 1999, told cabinet ministers and provincial government leaders that South Africa's economy had turned the corner towards improved growth.
But he said growth of three percent a year was not enough to create the jobs necessary to begin to reduce the country's unemployment rate, which some estimate at up to 40 percent.
"Changes in the non-agricultural sector of the economy and in the manufacturing sector in particular are well underway, reflecting the changes that the GEAR is designed to sustain.
"Overall, employment losses are tapering off, productivity is rising, unit labour costs are declining, capacity utilisation is increasing and private sector investment is increasing," he said.
Mbeki was speaking at a meeting of the quarterly Intergovernmental Forum meeting where provincial and national government leaders get together to harmonise their policies.

Mbeki, who oversees economic policy development and implementation, warned the provincial governments the GEAR, which has been criticised by unionists and left-wingers in the ruling African National Congress, was essential to the recovery of the country after decades of apartheid.
"Transformation of the economy along the lines envisaged in the GEAR must be pursued with renewed determination."
"But the structural changes required to achieve a higher growth rate of around six percent will pose many challenges and require tough decisions whose benefits may not be evident," he said.
The GEAR framework published in June last year combines labour market flexibility, supply-side strategies and fiscal discipline to achieve economic growth and job creation.
"We owe it to our people to succeed and thus cannot afford to pull in different directions. 1997 must see the acceleration of delivery in the area of social and economic infrastructure," he said.
